body:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by the T158 lane (PR #394) while splitting the artifact page's spawn clock. It is a READ-path defect, not a clock one, so it was deliberately left out of that diff — and the lane named it in the PR body but did NOT file a shard, so this ticket exists to stop the finding evaporating with the merge.

THE MECHANISM. The render path carries an EPOCH: a teardown bumps it, and an answer arriving from a superseded render is discarded rather than painted. The GESTURE path carries no such thing. So a mediated read that was in flight when a teardown ran lands in the FRESH map after it — the page answers a question the torn-down realm asked, into the world that replaced it.

AND THE ERASURE PATH HAS THE SAME HOLE, which is why this is not a cosmetic ordering nit. A read in flight across an erasure can deliver, into the post-erasure world, a value the erasure was supposed to make unreachable. That is the shape §11 exists to prevent: not bytes surviving at rest, but a READER seeing what the store no longer holds. Whether it is reachable in practice is the first thing to measure — do not assume either way.

BEFORE BUILDING, MEASURE, per the discipline T158 itself followed: drive the real page, put a mediated read in flight, tear down (and separately, erase) underneath it, and record whether the stale answer lands. A finding that cannot be reproduced is a hypothesis; say so and close the ticket if that is what the evidence shows.

THE REPAIR, if measurement earns it: give the gesture and erasure read paths the same epoch discipline the render path already has — an answer names the world it was asked in, and a world that no longer exists discards it. Prefer reusing the existing epoch rather than minting a second notion of currency; two clocks that must agree are a defect waiting to happen (T139 and T158 are both instances of exactly that).

RAILS: two-sided at both levels — a read in flight across a teardown does NOT land in the fresh map, AND an ordinary read still answers. Same pair across an erasure, with the erasure rail written so it fails if the stale value is served. Per the standing erasure rule every erasure rail is two-sided: the target is unreachable AND a named live bystander still reads.

WHO MERGES: if the fix only discards a stale answer, it makes a report more honest and self-merges on the ordinary bar. If it changes what any reader can observe across an erasure, that is Myk's — say which in one line in the PR.
title: A mediated read in flight survives a teardown — the gesture path has no epoch, and the erasure path has the same hole
